'''AQH share''' is a statistic that measures [[radio broadcasting|broadcast radio]] listenership.

==Definition==

{{dfni|AQH}} is an abbreviation for ''average quarter-hour persons'', defined by [[Arbitron]] (now referred to as Nielsen Audio) as the average number of persons listening to a particular station for at least five minutes during a 15-minute period.
{{dfni|Share}} is the percentage of those listening to radio in an Arbitron "market" (typically a [[metropolitan area]]) who are listening to a particular radio station.
Thus, {{dfni|AQH Share}} for a given station is mathematically expressed as:
<math display="block">\frac{\text{AQH persons listening to station}}{\text{AQH persons listening to all market radio stations}} \times 100\%</math>

==Usage==

AQH Share is most often used in conjunction with [[Time spent listening|TSL]] (Time Spent Listening) to measure listenership in a market. While AQH measures the average number of listeners to the station, TSL tracks the length of time listeners are tuned continuously to the station.
